text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Nottingham Forest and West Ham!
As we near kick off at the City Ground, how about some context around the two sides? Nottingham Forest are in 16th place on 21 points, just two points ahead of the drop zone with 14 matches to play.
Nottingham Forest also lost their last Premier League match 3-2 at home against Newcastle United, extending their winless streak to four (W0 D1 L3).
West Ham slumped 6-0 against Arsenal at London Stadium in their last Premier League match, extending their winless streak to five (W0 D3 L2), putting them in eighth place on 36 points.
The Hammers have scored 36 goals and conceded 42 through 24 matches, leaving them trailing fifth-placed Aston Villa by 10 points for a spot in the Europa League.
For the hosts Nottingham Forest, boss Nuno Espirito Santo has opted for two changes from the side that were beaten 3-2 by Newcastle on Saturday.
Danilo comes into the team for Ryan Yates while Felipe takes Moussa Niakhate's place in defence.
For the travelling contingent, West Ham's drubbing at the hands of Arsenal will ideally be put to bed by the end of today's game.
David Moyes has made two changes to that side that were handed the heavy 6-0 defeat by the Gunners on Sunday.
Michail Antonio makes his first start since November as Ben Johnson drops to the bench.
Kalvin Phillips starts in midfield with Tomas Soucek taking a place among the substitutes.
So, to today's officials...
The Referee is Tom Bramall, his Assistant Referees are Mat Wilkes and Adrian Holmes.
The Fourth Official is Gavin Ward and on VAR is Tim Robinson.
We're moments away from kick-off at the City Ground!
KICK OFF.
Referee Bramall gets us underway here and immediately Michail Antonio surges forward with intriguing link up from the right.
After a swarming break forward, Forest's early intentions are clear.
Gibbs-White is challenged strongly.
In the next phase Hudson-Odoi is aggressive.
Tavares chips a cross into Elanga who sees a low effort saved by Areola.
West Ham have to clear off the line!
Early end to end action is contributing to a raucous atmosphere here in Nottingham.
Jarrod Bowen causes problems, yet can't evade a Neco Williams block.
Kudus finds himself in with a yellow card.
The Ghanaian's energy is a little too overbearing and he earns himself a booking.
Gibbs-White rises to the tempo here and joins Kudus in the book for a reckless challenge.
The home side soak up a solid spell of West Ham pressure and try to break.
That final ball isn't there unfortunately, and Bowen tries to surge on the other way.
Alas, it's a shared theme.
Awoniyi against Zouma looks to be an intriguing battle - the Nigerian tries to turn his marker but a bundle insues.
All clean fun, the ref decides, no cards presented.
Forest are looking dangerous.
However, like most attacks, it's relatively reactive.
There's a limp penalty shout for a handball after a Williams low cross hits his sliding marker.
It's ignored and epitomises a very quick (although stop-start) match so far.
After a wasted, short Gibbs-White corner.
Kudus snuffs out the danger.
The next phase finds a lofted ball over - Antonio is a handfull and wins a free kick.
Ward-Prowse takes it sideways and again, we're into a common pattern of conservative possession.
The build-up is then disrupted by a marvelous Williams tackle.
The microphones picked that one up nicely.

While West Ham are in possession, it's worth noting that the Hammers are looking to complete a first league double over Nottingham Forest since 2011-12 in the Championship, and their first in the top-flight since 1968-69.
'Never lose it' - as we near 27 minutes it's a testament to the game's action that a David Moyes touch gets the crowd's attention.
Bowen strikes low, almost in anger! Not enough power unfortunately and Sels is hardly tested.

Approaching half an hour, a game of football has broken out! Dominguez stumbles over the ball, Gibbs-White gets on the rebounded block and forces a fine reaction stop from Areola! Up the other end, Antonio is free - but has too much time.
He gets tackled easily.
Frustrating...
The feet of Areola come to West Ham's rescue! Elanga slides a delightful ball in behind and Awoniyi looks destined to score.
However, the French 'keeper flies out excellently to offer a slide tackle his centre backs would be proud of.
And breathe...
Racing in behind is yet another common theme between the two sides.
Kudus is proving to be a bolt of energy for the visitors.
It's clear he'll likely be involved in anything positive Moyes' side can muster.

In their 6-0 defeat against Arsenal, West Ham had their joint-fewest shots (5), fewest shots on target (1), registered their lowest xG (0.2) and had their fewest touches in the opposition box (7) in a Premier League game this season.
Of course, not pleasant reading, yet there's been a markedly better showing already today - even if Antonio's composure appears to have been left on the team coach.
It's a booking for that man who's struggled for game time of late.
Michail Antonio is clearly frustrated and falls foul to a battle with Murillo.
He contests the decision.
His Brazilian opponent whips the crowd up.
This seems an inadvertent distraction from Hudson-Odoi's injury concern at the halfway line.
Gibbs-White now unsure too, as Emerson clatters him.
Speaking of Hudson-Odoi - he's ok now compared to a hobbling Gibbs-White.
Hudson-Odoi has scored a goal in each of his last two Premier League appearances for Nottingham Forest, as many as he’d scored in his first previous 43 matches combined.
It is the only time Hudson-Odoi has found the net in consecutive Premier League games.
Being on target again would be welcome here, as Gibbs-White moves gingerly after treatment.
Half chance here.
Elanga is lively down the right and pulls a flighted ball back to the edge of the box.
Danilo can't connect and it trickles through to Areola.
Five minutes have been added on for stoppages.
A swinging Hudson-Odoi arm has caught Coufal in the face.
There's been no foul given as the home fans bay for a booking for the Czech defender.
That said, they've not seen his bloodied lip.
We have a stoppage here, as the no.
five gets cleaned up.
West Ham can't get a corner routine right from Ward-Prowse.
The penalty spot crowd disperses but Forest manage to clear.
Tavares darts away on the break, but Phillips hits him with a peach of a challenge.
The ball to man ratio was perfect.
Assist Nicolás Martín Domínguez
GOOOOOAAALLLLLLL AWONIYIIII! Forest keep moving forwards.
Hudson-Odoi recycles the ball on the left back to his wing-counterpart Tavares.
The ball is floated back in and Awoniyi gets played in by Dominguez with a nicely weighted pass.
The big forward is ice cold to slot past a sprawling Areola.
He's scored in his last six outings against the Hammers.
Awoniyi clearly enjoyed that one! Ripping his shirt off, he picks up the expected yellow card.
He likely won't care though, as he's notched his sixth goal this season.
HALF-TIME: NOTTINGHAM FOREST 1-0 WEST HAM
Well, it's been a game that's taken its time to (really) wake up from a Saturday mid-afternoon doze, yet at the break we can reflect on Nottingham Forest leading West Ham by a goal-to-nil.
There were half chances galore for a spell, as Anthony Elanga was left frustrated by Alphonse Areola's sharp reflexes early on.
Then, after a bleak Jarrod Bowen pea-roller, the half-hour mark saw a crescendo of action as Morgan Gibbs-White forced another fine Areola stop before Antonio at the other end couldn't stay composed.
Areola was close to West Ham's best player, but would've been frustrated to concede on the brink of the break.
Taiwo Awoniyi was slotted in by Nicolas Dominguez and was brilliant to get his sixth goal of the term.
Antonio has come into the fray with his noticeable physical presence.
However, with West Ham's dire recent exploits - his lack of composure needs to subside if the visitors have any chance of getting back in to this one.
The link up play needs to be better too - Antonio attempted just 4 passes in the first half.
He's been marshalled excellently by those in red.
SECOND HALF KICK OFF: We're back underway at the City Ground.
Where we'd looked at Areola as West Ham's best player, the Frenchman looks to continue in the same vein straight away! Elanga latches on to a floated ball and volleys superbly from the right.
It's an expected, yet brilliant stop from Areola who tips over in agile fashion.
The resulting corner reaps nothing.
Despite being under pressure, West Ham will be driven by the fact that when it comes to securing points from losing positions - the Hammers sit sixth with 11.
While they look to come from behind - maybe Bowen might be the talisman.
He has netted on 11 occasions.
He is tied for fifth for goals scored in the league in 2023-24.
Kurt Zouma stops an exciting Forest breakaway.
It wasn't really a tackle he needed to make (hence the yellow card) yet his lacklustre defensive counterparts will likely thank him for the momentary respite.
Antonio has come out in this second half with intent.
Latching onto a pinpoint switch of play, the boisterous front man looks to restock his confidence as he drives as Williams off the left wing.
The former Liverpool man is second best and can only foul his adversary.
The resulting free kick is deep in Ward-Prowse country, yet he can't get the dip and swerve right from just outside the box.
It has Sels flying, but still clears the crossbar comfortably.
Forest don't deal with possession on the edge of their box and Bowen bursts out.
He forces another simple stop from Sels.
That said, it's encouraging for fans of the east London outfit.
Up the other end, Murillo lofts over a delightful ball in the channel for Hudson-Odoi.
He cuts back inside and crosses for Awoniyi, but the forward gets under it with his header.
Awoniyi makes way for Divock Origi.
His goal is the difference maker so far.
If he can keep firing, Forest will no doubt feel better about the looming questions of survival amidst the bottom half scrummage.
Phillips is fouled, yet as he's down, Dominguez tries to wrestle the ball free.
It's a classic game-slowing tactic, yet the Manchester City loanee takes exception and shoves the Argentinian.
All parties are booked, including Coufal who had some unsavoury thoughts as well.
Nicolas Dominguez gets his reward for the pantomime villain role.
Coufal carded - the Czech international takes a warning for standing up for his teammate Phillips.
Danilo strikes a thumping volley as the ball falls from height on the edge of the box.
It's a venomous effort, yet Areola parries away with relative ease.
PHILLIPS WALKS...
Gibbs-White makes the most of a hot-headed Phillips challenge and as the Forest midfielder is caught by his marker, the ref's second yellow is already out of the pocket.
On his second start for West Ham, Phillips receives his marching orders, ultimately falling foul to Dominguez and that petulant booking just minutes earlier.
West Ham will do well to arrest this downward slide.
Moyes is turning to what looks like a triple change here.
Well, the subs have been confirmed.
It's two changes, instead of the previously thought three.
A formerly bloodied Coufal makes way for Ben Johnson.
Antonio has got 75 minutes under his belt on his return.
Maxwel Cornet emerges - can he make the difference here?
Tavares strikes...
and it's still rising.
It's an audacious effort from the Arsenal-loanee from around 25-yards.
It might still be flying as we speak.
Forest are enjoying themselves it seems.
Hudson-Odoi does well down the left.
He guides it back for Elanga, but he hits it higher than Tavares! What a waste.
OOHHHH COULD WE SEE A PENALTY HERE?? Williams zips down the right side of the box and substitute Cornet has seemingly stepped on the Welshman's standing leg from behind.
We're deep in VAR discourse with Tim Robinson until referee Bramall makes his own mind up.
We play on...
As one has previously departed, our Czech quota for the day is replenished.
Soucek arrives for Emerson.
On his third Premier League start, Sels has hardly been tested.
This continues as a wishful strike from range hardly stings the palms.
The hosts have a corner here and it looks as if the hosts will avoid their fifth straight game without a victory as they reinforce from the bench.
Nicolas Dominguez makes way for Ryan Yates.
He mouths 'good game hermano'.
It's been a good game indeed for Forest so far!
GOAL?? No! In a chaotic sequence, Danilo strikes from range and it spins off a body.
Areola can't grasp the looping ball and it falls in.
Referee ends the celebrations - Yates was lurking in an offside position.
West Ham are looking to salvage something here but Forest survive a Ward-Prowse free kick from the left.
The ball gets recycled relentlessly but there are Hammers astray behind the offside line.
Forest hearts are in mouths, and they'll continue to be for another six minutes of added time.
Danilo blocks for Forest late on and Ward-Prowse's corner isn't utilised.
The hosts break but dear oh dear - Elanga must have gravity boots on! His shot skyrockets off target, leaving a sour, pip-ridden cherry sliding off the top of a frenetic Forest fastbreak
The attacking impetus is clear for Moyes and co.
Danny Ings on for Zouma - could he be the saviour?
Gibbs-White's solid performance comes to an end as Andrew Omobamidele takes his place to strengthen the defence in the dying embers.

GOOOAAAAALLLL HUDSON-ODOI SEALS IT AT THE DEATH! For his third successive appearance in the Premier League, the Chelsea graduate mops up the pieces as West Ham can't clear from a devilish low byline drive from Williams on the right.
It goes through Elanga but Hudson-Odoi makes sure the game's well and truly over, slamming into the bottom left corner!
It's down as an Elanga assist, but ultimately Williams did the heavy lifting with a surging run!
FULL TIME: NOTTINGHAM FOREST 2-0 WEST HAM
There we go, it's all over on the banks of the Trent as Nottingham Forest experience double delight over a bereft West Ham with a 2-0 victory that could be crucial in their hopes of survival.
It was a forgettable day for David Moyes' side as Mats Sels was hardly tested in the hosts' goal.
Alphonse Areola however, was the polar opposite, and was kept busy for much of the game.
He would've been approaching the break with optimism, as well as being a shoe-in for West Ham's player of the match, however Taiwo Awoniyi had other ideas.
He grabbed his sixth goal of the season on the cusp of half time before the second, frenetic half took a while for Forest to grab a late insurance goal.
This came after a penalty shout, and Danilo's effort were denied by the referee's whistle.
Callum Hudson-Odoi was composed to slot home emphatically to send Forest fans home happy - five points clear of the dropzone.
West Ham continue their slump as they prepare for Brentford next.
Nottingham Forest however, surge on to face Aston Villa next time out.
Thanks for following along, goodbye!
